title: Deterministic bonsai growth
problem: There is no bounded, reproducible tree model that maps weekly activity to visible growth.
action_items: Read the relevant installed Next guide before touching route code in later tasks; implement a pure bracketed L-system in lib/bonsai.ts using ISO-week plus counts as the seed, tapered strokes, stable branch IDs, parent links, node cap, and log-scaled branch/leaf density.
Make zero-count weeks add bare twigs and prevent a quiet week from deleting prior growth; add unit fixtures for identical seeds, differing weeks, empty weeks, branch ancestry and node cap.
acceptance_criteria: The same week and contribution snapshot always produce identical bounded tree geometry; quiet weeks leave bare twigs and every pruneable branch has a stable subtree identity.

title: Build time contribution snapshot
problem: The site has no reliable owner activity snapshot for build-time tree growth.
action_items: Implement an on-demand scripts/fetch-contributions.mjs command that reads public activity for the pinned owner quiinthieu, aggregates by ISO week, validates count/date bounds, writes only counts and provenance, and exits usefully on malformed data.

Commit a real baseline content/contributions.json captured from public activity and make the build use it when refresh fails; a failed network request must not make page load perform a fetch or fabricate current activity.
Test the parser and refresh path with local fixtures including zero weeks, incomplete current week, invalid response and network failure; document the explicit refresh command and snapshot age.
acceptance_criteria: Running the refresh command updates a validated owner weekly-count snapshot from public activity; offline builds use the committed snapshot with its as-of date and never fetch on page load.

title: Interactive seasonal Ink Bonsai
problem: Visitors cannot see or interact with the owner activity tree.
action_items: Read installed Next route guidance; build /play/bonsai and a Play entry using the committed snapshot and lib/bonsai output, existing SVG ink filters, responsive light/dark styling and site data-season.
Render spring blossom, summer green leaves, autumn red leaves and winter bare/snow states; expose week/count/source and an honest snapshot age.

Make branch targets at least 24px with mouse, touch, Enter and Space pruning; remove the selected subtree, animate falling ink leaves only when motion is allowed, synthesize a gesture-gated snip through the existing sound setting, and offer Regrow.
Add browser coverage for zero-week twig, one-branch pruning/regrowth, keyboard focus, all seasons, reduced motion and mute; ensure no request to GitHub on page load.
acceptance_criteria: The Bonsai page shows deterministic owner growth and four seasonal treatments; a visitor can prune and regrow by pointer or keyboard, with gated sound and a static reduced-motion outcome.

title: Bonsai week postcard
problem: A tree of the week cannot yet be shared as a consistent image.
action_items: Read the installed Next image route guide; implement /og/bonsai?week=YYYY-Www using the same pure tree model and snapshot, a bounded week parser, and flat ink style compatible with next/og without relying on SVG filter support.
Add a postcard PNG download from the browser using the visible week's tree, date, count and source; make unsupported canvas/export fail with a useful message rather than a broken link.
Add tests for identical image content at the same week, invalid-week fallback, nonblank PNG, and no cross-origin assets.
acceptance_criteria: A valid week URL serves a shareable deterministic OG image, and the Bonsai page downloads a nonblank matching PNG postcard; invalid weeks fail safely.

title: Pinned hand model assets
problem: The theatre cannot run privately offline without a verified local Hand Landmarker model.
action_items: Follow the existing Peep Box vendor pattern for the pinned @mediapipe/tasks-vision 0.10.32 Hand Landmarker model: immutable source, SHA256, byte size, license and local public URL; vendor only the required model and wasm assets.

Add fail-closed manifest/hash checks and verify an actual HandLandmarker import and asset/adapter construction with the pinned package in the locked npm environment, plus a wrong-hash negative control.
acceptance_criteria: The pinned local model and runtime assets pass hash and license checks, construct with the locked MediaPipe package, and a corrupt asset fails verification.

title: Opt in hand tracking
problem: No reusable theatre tracker handles consent, lifecycle or model failures.
action_items: Implement an opt-in only controller around getUserMedia({audio:false}) and MediaPipe VIDEO mode for up to two hands, with worker execution, GPU attempt and CPU fallback, bounded detection near 20Hz, mirrored coordinates, cleanup on stop/unmount/hidden/revoke and no retained frames.
Keep the permission request behind an explicit user button; expose start/stop/error states and a fallback signal. Use local model/wasm URLs only.

Test camera never starts on import, denied permission, GPU failure/CPU success, aborted startup, visibility loss, track stop and cleanup using fakes; run a real import/adapter preflight against locked assets.
acceptance_criteria: Camera access begins only after a visitor opts in; tracking stays in-browser, uses local assets, handles CPU fallback and releases tracks on every exit path.

title: Four shadow pose classifier
problem: Raw hand landmarks do not provide stable rabbit, dog, bird or deer poses.
action_items: Implement mirrored landmark normalization, bounded One Euro smoothing, geometry-based pose scores for rabbit/dog/bird/deer (one or two hands as appropriate), six-frame debounce and exit hysteresis; emit neutral when confidence is low.

Add recorded or synthetic 21-point landmark fixtures for all four poses, left/right mirror, rapid transitions, missing hand, ambiguous hand and negative controls; keep classifier pure and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: All four requested poses resolve from landmark fixtures with stable transitions, while ambiguous or missing hands remain neutral.

title: Ink shadow theatre stage
problem: Visitors cannot turn recognized poses into creatures and useful links.
action_items: Read installed Next client/route guidance; build /play/shadows and its Play entry with a clear pre-consent privacy notice: local processing, no upload or saving, and a Stop control.

Draw landmark-derived palm/finger ink silhouettes on a paper stage with candle glow; morph matched-point SVG creatures for rabbit, dog, bird and deer, and give each a bounded hop plus a paper tag carrying a Projects or Notes link. Keep semantic anchors below the stage.
Respect site light/dark styling and reduced motion with static candle and in-place creature swap; never render webcam video or start/fetch model before opt-in.
Add browser checks for notice-before-permission, each creature via fixture injection, Stop releasing camera, keyboard link access, reduced motion, and absence of frame/network upload.
acceptance_criteria: After explicit consent, four poses appear as ink creatures on the paper stage, carry working Projects/Notes links, and Stop releases the camera; reduced motion stays static.

title: Drag paper cutout puppets
problem: Visitors without a camera or permission cannot use the theatre.
action_items: Add an always-selectable paper cutout mode using the same four creature assets and links, with pointer/touch drag constrained to the stage plus arrow-key movement and visible focus.
Automatically enter this mode on denial, insecure context, unsupported browser or model failure; offer a mode switch without requesting permission.
Test pointer and keyboard placement, each failure path, no camera call in cutout mode, touch behavior, and reduced-motion state.
acceptance_criteria: All four cutout puppets can be moved by mouse, touch or keyboard and carry the same links; camera denial or model failure lands in a usable fallback.

title: Privacy and regression gate
problem: The new routes need a complete independent regression path and named CI gate coverage.
action_items: Extend e2e for initial zero camera prompts, no cross-origin model/frame requests, opt-in with Chromium fake camera, model/permission denial, four fixture poses, cutout fallback, both link destinations, Bonsai seasonal/prune/postcard paths and reduced motion.
Name the added e2e tests in scripts/check-gate-closure.mjs and demonstrate the gate rejects a temporarily renamed required test, restoring the tree afterward.
Run project unit, lint, typecheck, build and browser gates at the delivery SHA; record local fake-device limits, locked model hash and independent browser observations for QA.
interfaces: e2e/bonsai.test.ts; e2e/bonsai-postcard.test.ts; e2e/shadows.test.ts; e2e/shadow-puppets.test.ts; scripts/check-gate-closure.mjs; lib/gate-closure.test.ts
non_goals: live camera recognition as CI proof
acceptance_criteria: CI names and runs the new privacy, interaction, fallback and share checks; a renamed required test makes gate closure fail, and the complete project checks pass.
